rounds.response: Short summary: fever 38.3°C, mild tachycardia (HR 108) and 10 hours of progressive focal RLQ tenderness are concerning for early appendicitis but he is hemodynamically stable and has no peritonitis on exam. Consider urgent diagnostics (CBC ± differential, CRP, urinalysis, and regional imaging—ultrasound if young/lean or CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast if diagnostic uncertainty or higher BMI) and keep him NPO with analgesia/anti-emetic as needed while awaiting results. Monitor vitals and repeat abdominal exam q30–60 minutes; escalate to higher-acuity bed and surgical review if increasing pain, signs of peritonitis, hypotension, rising tachycardia (e.g., >120), or worsening labs. Your plan to keep him in the standard queue is reasonable provided you can obtain prompt assessment/imaging within ~60–120 minutes and perform frequent reassessments. If rapid imaging or serial exams will be delayed, consider upgrading acuity until those are complete.
